driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of 5 October 2026 after the GitHub Actions pre-open fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-10-02.json from Friday 2 October's close. Every figure is dated at or before the 2026-10-02 close; news-log entries dated 3 and 4 October (Houthi/Aramco, OPEC+ hold, Camp David meeting) were deliberately not used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched and were carried stale: bonds 15 (TLT 30-day implied volatility, 25 September), dollar 4.72 (EUR/USD 1-month implied volatility, 21 September), IWM 19.97 (RVX, 23 September). No newer prints were obtainable.

Source conflicts on 2 October: the news log has the 10-year yield at 5.18% (-6bp) and S&P 500 at 7,720.44, while the investingLive wrap shows the 10-year at 5.2939% (+6bp, yields 'reversed higher') and S&P 500 at 7,722.85; gold GC=F closed -0.08% on the drafted close while the wrap shows spot gold -0.83%; WTI is -4.22% pre-market in the news log vs -1.57% to $91.41 at the close in the wrap. Votes use drafted closes and avoid contested yield levels.

No 2 October high-yield OAS, MOVE, breadth counts or positioning print was obtainable; credit, breadth, positioning and volatility votes are neutral where no dated figure exists. AAII (32.7/19.2/48.1) is the week to 23 September. Seasonality votes are neutral because no dated sourced statistic was obtained.

Fed odds: October hike probability fell to roughly 15-16% after the payrolls miss (from 64% a week earlier per the news log); one economist quoted by Yahoo still called the late-October decision 'live'.

News-log entries for 2026-10-02 (payrolls +29K, crude slide, record Nasdaq close, Mideast troop deployment, Nike) were already in data/news_log.json; the Artifact database returned the same five entries. No hand-entered issue entries were dated 2 October.

newsLog.event: September nonfarm payrolls come in at just +29K, far below consensus, unemployment rate ticks up to 4.2%; bond traders slash October Fed rate-hike odds
newsLog.numbers: NFP +29K; unemployment 4.2% (prior 4.1%); AHE +3.2% y/y; July revised to -10K, Aug to +133K; 10Y 5.18%, 30Y 5.57%; Oct hike odds 16% (64% a week ago)
newsLog.reaction: Weak labor data pared Fed hike bets: yields fell, gold up, equity futures jumped (S&P +0.9%, Nasdaq +1.35%, Dow +0.94%)
newsLog.tickers: SPY, QQQ, TLT, 10Y, yield, Treasury, GLD, gold
newsLog.vsExp: Miss: consensus roughly +84K to +90K (sources differ); unemployment expected 4.1%; AHE in line

newsLog.event: Crude oil falls sharply pre-market as Brent drops back to about $99/bbl, easing some inflation pressure alongside weak jobs data
newsLog.numbers: WTI Nov -4.22% to $88.95; Brent ~$99 (-2.6% on the day, up ~54% y/y); catalyst n/a
newsLog.reaction: Lower crude supports the rate-relief move in yields and equity futures; still elevated vs a year ago

newsLog.event: S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq close higher as soft September jobs report cements dovish Fed outlook; Nasdaq sets a fresh record close on AI/Nvidia strength
newsLog.numbers: S&P 500 7,720.44 (+0.70%); Dow 51,143.70 (+0.43%); Nasdaq Composite 27,179.15 (+1.14%, record close); 10Y Treasury yield 5.18% (-6bps)
newsLog.reaction: Nvidia hit a fresh intraday record (~$237.88, market cap above $5.7T); risk-on tone extended after weak payrolls cut October Fed hike odds to roughly 16-18%

newsLog.event: Trump deploys roughly 9,000 troops and the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group to the Middle East, warns Iran will be "hit very hard"; a third carrier could arrive by late October
newsLog.numbers: ~9,000 troops; USS Theodore Roosevelt CSG + USS Makin Island ARG; total regional presence could exceed 20,000 sailors/Marines
newsLog.reaction: Oil stayed elevated on Middle East tension (Brent roughly $99-102/bbl depending on source) even as the broader tape rallied on rate-cut hopes; raises tail risk for energy prices

newsLog.event: Nike slides after a fiscal Q1 revenue miss and weak outlook; management flags upcoming layoffs as part of cost-cutting
newsLog.reaction: Shares fell against an otherwise strong tape as investors weighed the soft guidance and planned layoffs
